problem_type: APIMart canonical model identity and reference-cardinality drift
symptom: Curated mappings sent legacy or internal APIMart model identifiers, and the Omni reference mapping could submit the documented-invalid two-image combination instead of failing before spend.
direct_cause: Model identity was copied from historical catalog keys directly into the wire body, while the shared template path had no model-specific validator for APIMart's Omni 1-or-3 image contract.
class_root: The earliest shared APIMart request boundary did not own the provider's canonical model-ID translation and model-specific reference invariants; each mapping could therefore drift independently while local construction still looked valid.
affected_population: APIMart Seedream 4.5 and 5.0 Pro image mappings
APIMart Seedance 2.0 and 2.5, Grok Imagine 1.5, and Omni Flash video mappings
Users submitting Omni with two reference images, which the official contract rejects synchronously
entry_points: APIMART_IMAGE_MODELS imageCreateOp for Seedream 4.5 and Seedream 5.0 Pro
APIMART_VIDEO_MODELS videoCreateOp for Seedance 2.0/2.5, Grok Imagine 1.5, and Omni Flash
validateProfileRequestBeforeSpend and the final request transform immediately before HTTP

external_sources.purpose: Defines the current canonical model id seedream-4.5 and the flat image generation fields.
Defines the current canonical model id seedream-5-0-pro and the 1K/1.5K/2K resolution contract.
Defines seedance-2.0/fast/mini IDs and image_urls versus image_with_roles mutual exclusion.
Defines canonical seedance-2.5 and the reference/first-last constraints.
Defines canonical gemini-omni-1.1-flash-ext, generation_type, and the supported one-or-three image counts.

invariants: Every APIMart mapping covered by the translation table sends the official canonical model ID on the wire, while internal legacy catalog keys remain readable for existing projects.
The Omni mapping accepts zero images for text mode and exactly one or three images for reference mode; two or four-plus images fail before localization or spend.
The same validator runs in the pre-spend validation path and in the final request transform, so a future caller cannot bypass the contract by skipping one path.
All current KIE/APIMart mappings can be constructed in a zero-network dry run without unresolved template placeholders or cross-vendor endpoint leakage.
generality_proof: All affected mappings converge on the APIMart create operation and the same pre-spend/final-transform lifecycle. Translating IDs and validating Omni cardinality at that shared boundary prevents a new caller, legacy catalog row, or future mapping from reintroducing the same wire drift through a second hand-written branch.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Translate documented APIMart IDs and fail closed on Omni reference cardinality before spend and again before HTTP.
Attach the named boundary to every affected APIMart video mapping from the single video factory.
Attach the named canonical-ID boundary to affected APIMart image mappings from the single image factory.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both Seedream 4.5 and 5.0 Pro mappings copied legacy doubao-prefixed keys into the body; both official pages specify seedream-* canonical IDs.
The official video pages specify canonical IDs different from the historical catalog keys; Omni also has a unique 1-or-3 image invariant.
The official pages specify wan2.7 and wan3.0-video, exactly matching the current wire model values; they remain covered by the all-mapping dry run.

recurrence.reason: APIMart model pages and historical catalog identities can drift independently, and any future reference-capable model can have a cardinality or mutual-exclusion rule that generic templates cannot infer.
same_class_scan: Enumerated all 49 APIMart mappings from applyBuiltinSeeds and all 32 KIE mappings; compared every model/body endpoint and reference-bearing mapping against the official pages listed above.
Checked all APIMart video factories and the image factory for legacy model prefixes, plus the shared request lifecycle validateProfileRequestBeforeSpend/final applyRequestTransform.
Checked Omni text, one-image, two-image, and three-image cases; only one and three are accepted by the official Omni page, so two is a fail-closed regression case.
Checked Wan 2.7, Wan 3.0, H3, Sora, Veo, Kling, Hailuo, Vidu, audio, and KIE mappings as unaffected or already guarded; their fields remain in the dry-run test.

prevention.invariant: Affected APIMart model IDs are canonicalized and Omni reference cardinality is 0, 1, or 3 only.
prevention.failure_mode: Invalid Omni references throw a stable validation error before spend; the final transform repeats the same validation as defense in depth.
prevention.strategy: Use named request transforms attached by the existing model/image/video factories so every affected mapping shares one boundary and no caller-specific fallback remains.

legacy_paths.rationale: The historical catalog identifiers remain as migration-safe internal keys; only their outgoing wire value is corrected at the shared request boundary. No parallel HTTP implementation or fallback path is retained.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The fix uses the existing request-transform registry and no third-party dependency controls the provider contract.

migration: Existing projects and catalog records keep their historical modelKey values so routing and persisted node identity do not change. When a request is built, only the outgoing APIMart model field is canonicalized; no stored key or external credential is rewritten.
residual_risks: APIMart accepts some historical aliases, so live acceptance of an alias is not proof that it remains documented or stable; the matrix records canonical wire values separately.

The APIMart docs do not expose a free universal model-list endpoint in the fetched manual; the free probes therefore validate documented endpoints and parameter errors, not a complete account-specific availability list.

The two accidental 200 probe submissions are not used as acceptance evidence; their exact task IDs were not persisted by the old probe script, so any provider-side settlement remains part of the honest spend uncertainty recorded in the final report.
